title: Taxi, Sedan, or SUV for Your Airport Transfer? What Actually Matters
detailHtml:
Most of the "which ground transportation should I book" advice out there focuses on image — taxi versus limo, standard versus luxury. In practice, the decision usually comes down to three things: how many people are traveling, how much luggage you're bringing, and what the trip costs you if it goes wrong.

Group size and luggage drive the vehicle choice

A sedan works fine for one or two travelers with carry-ons. Once you're a family of four with checked bags, or a small group traveling together, a larger vehicle stops being a luxury and starts being the only practical option — splitting a group across two cars costs more and adds coordination you don't need before a flight. Our fleet includes a Cadillac Escalade IQ for larger groups, a Honda CR-V for a smaller, easy-to-park option, and a Kia EV9 if you'd like an all-electric ride.

What actually protects your trip

The thing that matters more than the vehicle itself is what happens when a flight is early, late, or cancelled. Every airport ride we run includes flight tracking, so pickup timing adjusts automatically instead of you re-booking or waiting on hold. Pricing is flat and quoted up front — no surge charges for landing during a storm or a holiday weekend. See our comparison with Uber and Lyft for more on how that differs from an app-dispatched ride.

Booking for a group or an event

If you're coordinating transportation for a wedding party, a business trip, or a group staying at a nearby hotel, call ahead with your group size and timeline so we can line up the right vehicle. See our wedding guest transportation and corporate transportation pages for details on those specifically.
